rationale: Evidence from iteration 2 (base_speed 1.2, kp 3.0, kd 0.3, ki 0.1, sensor_size 0.016): still 0 finishes in 60 trials. line_loss_events stayed at 1.0 (1.05 on the oval) and max_error stayed at 0.062 to 0.064, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit. Lowering base_speed did not remove line loss, so speed is not the main cause. Geometry is the likely cause. With sensors at x = -0.04 to +0.04 and a 0.016 m footprint, the outermost sensor stops seeing the 25 mm tape once the robot's centre is about 0.04 + 0.0125 + 0.008 = 0.0605 m off the line. That is the same as the off-track limit, so the robot reads zero signal at the moment it fails. Widening the span to ±0.07 m should keep some sensor on the tape out to roughly 0.08 m, so line loss should only occur after the robot has already left, or not at all. Oscillation also rose to 0.30 on the oval (from 0.24 at kp 3.5) and 0.28 on the s-bend, above the 0.2 level. The Evaluator's listed next step is to raise kd toward 0.45 when oscillation stays above 0.2 at kp 3.0. Changes: (1) sensor x positions widened to -0.07, -0.035, 0, 0.035, 0.07 (spacing 0.035 m, footprint 0.016 m, so adjacent footprints still overlap the tape); (2) kd 0.3 to 0.45 to damp the jitter. base_speed 1.2, kp 3.0, ki 0.1, sensor_weights, sensor_size, body, wheel and mass are unchanged. I accept that two changes in one race confound the result. I chose this because the iteration budget is limited, and the two symptoms are separate: line loss relates to span and oscillation relates to damping. Expected result: line_loss_events falls well below 1.0, max_error falls below 0.06 on the oval and s-bend, steering_oscillation falls below 0.2, and progress rises above 0.6 on the oval. Completion within 3 s is still unlikely at 1.2. Hypotheses to test: (a) line_loss_events drops toward 0 with the wider span; (b) kd 0.45 brings steering_oscillation under 0.2; (c) with the robot kept on the line, the next lever is base_speed 1.3 then 1.4 to reach completion_time under 3 s. If line_loss_events is still 1.0 with the wider span, the cause is probably not sensor span, and the next test should be sensor y position or sensor_size 0.012.
